title: Session-Based Authentication

searches.query: "Session-Based Authentication" interview session fixation logout distributed store
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: OWASP: Session Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Opaque session lifecycle, cookie scope, regeneration, expiry and server-side invalidation; flags do not replace authorization/CSRF controls.

sources.title: OWASP: Authentication Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Identity proof, reauthentication, safe responses and protection of authentication endpoints; deployment-specific choices remain explicit.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

sources.title: OWASP: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Context-specific encoding, safe sinks, maintained rich-HTML sanitization and CSP defense in depth.

sources.title: OWASP: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Framework token protection, signed/session-bound double submit, origin and SameSite defense boundaries; CORS is not universal CSRF protection.

scenarios.theme: A pre-login session identifier survives login. What do you change?
scenarios.assumptions: An attacker may have caused that identifier to be known before the victim authenticated. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A pre-login session identifier survives login. What do you change?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Regenerate the authenticated session using the supported framework transition, invalidate the old authority and migrate only required nonprivileged state.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Regeneration must handle concurrent requests and cart continuity

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Simply changing the displayed user name does not establish a fresh credential boundary.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to session; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Logout deletes the browser cookie but a copied cookie still works. What now?
scenarios.assumptions: The product promises that session is no longer usable after logout. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Session-Based Authentication to stolen cookie.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Logout deletes the browser cookie but a copied cookie still works. What now?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Invalidate the authoritative server session and relevant caches, expire the matching cookie scope and test the copied identifier after the promised cut-off

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Central invalidation has consistency and availability costs

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Already executing effects may need a separate fresh-check boundary; cookie deletion cannot cancel them.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to session, authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.theme: An active browser stays signed in forever. What lifetime was omitted?
scenarios.assumptions: Idle timers keep extending but policy requires a maximum authenticated session age. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Session-Based Authentication to timeout policy.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An active browser stays signed in forever. What lifetime was omitted?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Enforce an absolute lifetime alongside the idle policy on the server and use supported reauthentication/renewal behavior with clear user feedback.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: More reauthentication affects convenience

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: An absolute limit and an idle limit protect different exposure windows; cookie persistence alone cannot implement both correctly.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to session, authn; interview frequency is not claimed.

publicDisclosure: Researched 2026-11-17. These are adapted production scenarios informed by concept-specific interview searches and the named references below. The System Design Primer provides core orientation where applicable; technical guarantees use the mapped primary sources. Exact interview frequency, rankings and company attribution were not independently verified. Security protocol and runtime examples state their assumptions; the questions test reasoning rather than a universal product recommendation.
